### Study Design:
Single-center, ambispective observational study. Eligible subjects who previously underwent bilateral uncomplicated cataract surgery with implantation of the TECNIS Odyssey intraocular lens will be identified retrospectively. Each subject will participate in a single prospective postoperative study visit conducted at least three months after surgery. Cataract surgery itself is not part of the study.

### Endpoints:
Primary Endpoint:
- Photopic and mesopic visual acuity at distance (6 m), intermediate (66 cm), and near (40 cm and 33 cm) assessed at the postoperative study visit.

Secondary Endpoint:
- Patient-reported outcomes assessed using the Assessment of Intraocular Lens Implant Symptoms (AIOLIS) questionnaire.

Exploratory Endpoints:
- Correlation of postoperative quality-of-vision concerns with corneal performance index.
- Correlation of pupil size with patient satisfaction.

- Retrospective Component:
  Identification of eligible subjects through medical record review confirming prior bilateral cataract surgery with Odyssey IOL implantation.

  - Informed consent

  - Manifest refraction
  - Photopic and mesopic visual acuity testing at distance, intermediate, and near
  - Assessment of Intraocular Lens Implant Symptoms (AIOLIS)
  - Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI)
  - iTrace assessment
  - Pupil size measurement
  - Adverse event assessment

All study procedures are non-interventional and consistent with standard ophthalmic evaluations.

Study Start Date: March 1, 2025  
First Patient Enrolled: March 15, 2025  
Last Patient Completed: December 15, 2025  
Data Analysis: January 2026  
Final Report Submission: February 28, 2026

### Number of Sites:
One

### Background:
Multifocal and extended range of vision intraocular lenses have improved spectacle independence following cataract surgery; however, earlier designs have been associated with visual disturbances such as halos, glare, and reduced contrast sensitivity. This study aims to evaluate visual performance and patient satisfaction at least three months after surgery.

### Primary Objective:
To evaluate postoperative visual acuity outcomes following bilateral implantation of the TECNIS Odyssey intraocular lens.

Bilateral implantation of the TECNIS Odyssey intraocular lens provides good visual acuity at distance, intermediate, and near, with acceptable patient-reported visual quality and satisfaction.

### Study Title:
Ambispective Analysis of Patient Reported Outcomes and Visual Acuity in Patients with Bilateral Implantation of Odyssey Intraocular Lenses

### Study Design:
Single-center, ambispective observational study. Subjects who previously underwent bilateral uncomplicated cataract surgery with implantation of the TECNIS Odyssey intraocular lens will be identified retrospectively through medical record review. Each eligible subject will participate in a single prospective postoperative study visit conducted at least three months after surgery. Cataract surgery itself is not part of the study.

### Background:
Multifocal and extended range of vision intraocular lenses have improved spectacle independence following cataract surgery; however, earlier designs have been associated with visual disturbances such as halos, glare, and reduced contrast sensitivity. The TECNIS Odyssey intraocular lens was developed to provide a broader range of vision while maintaining visual quality. Although the Odyssey IOL is FDA approved and used in routine clinical practice, limited data are available regarding postoperative visual acuity and patient-reported outcomes following bilateral implantation. This study aims to further characterize visual performance and patient satisfaction at least three months after surgery.

### Primary Objective:
To evaluate postoperative visual acuity outcomes following bilateral implantation of the TECNIS Odyssey intraocular lens.

### Hypothesis:
Bilateral implantation of the TECNIS Odyssey intraocular lens provides good visual acuity at distance, intermediate, and near, with acceptable patient-reported visual quality and satisfaction.

### Endpoints:
Primary Endpoint:
- Photopic and mesopic visual acuity at distance (6 m), intermediate (66 cm), and near (40 cm and 33 cm) assessed at the postoperative study visit.

Secondary Endpoint:
- Patient-reported outcomes assessed using the Assessment of Intraocular Lens Implant Symptoms (AIOLIS) questionnaire.

Exploratory Endpoints:
- Correlation of postoperative quality-of-vision concerns with corneal performance index.
- Correlation of pupil size with patient satisfaction.

### Assessments Schedule:
- Retrospective Component:
  Identification of eligible subjects via medical record review confirming prior bilateral cataract surgery with Odyssey IOL implantation.

- Prospective Study Visit (≥ 3 months postoperatively):
  - Informed consent
  - Medical history
  - Manifest refraction
  - Photopic and mesopic visual acuity testing at distance, intermediate, and near
  - Assessment of Intraocular Lens Implant Symptoms (AIOLIS)
  - Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI)
  - iTrace assessment
  - Pupil size measurement
  - Adverse event assessment

All study procedures are non-interventional and consistent with standard ophthalmic evaluations.
